title: Mood changes during your cycle, explained
description: Explore mood changes during your menstrual cycle, what to note in a mood log, and when to ask for support, without fixed rules about how you should feel.
imageAlt: Blue Mochi with a thought bubble containing a pink heart
intro: Some people notice mood changes before a period, while others do not. Premenstrual symptoms differ between people and can change over time. A dated mood log can help you describe your experience, but it cannot diagnose the reason for it.

premenstrual-changes.title: What premenstrual changes can look like

paragraphs.first: PMS can include emotional symptoms such as irritability, anxiety, sadness or mood changes, alongside physical symptoms. Symptoms commonly occur before a period and ease after it starts.
paragraphs.second: A list of symptoms is not a test. If something is bothering you or affecting daily life, ask a healthcare professional about it.

useful-notes.title: Keep the notes specific to your day

items.date: Record the date and the mood words that feel right to you.
items.impact: Add a short note about how strongly it affected your day.
items.context: Include context you want to remember, such as sleep, stress or a difficult event.

useful-notes.after: You can log ordinary days too. A record that includes comfortable days is easier to discuss than a list made only when you felt bad.

avoid-rules.title: Avoid fixed rules about how you should feel

paragraphs.first: You do not need to feel energetic, social, calm or tired on a particular cycle day. Use a diary to record your own experience instead of fitting it to a template.
paragraphs.second: In Mochi, mood logging is optional. A mascot reaction is part of the app experience; it is not a medical interpretation of your entry.

support.title: Ask for support when you need it

paragraphs.first: If mood symptoms bother you, interfere with everyday life, or persist, speak with a qualified healthcare professional. Bring your notes if you find them helpful.
paragraphs.second: Do not wait to build a long record before asking for support. A diary is one way to explain what you noticed, not a requirement for care.

everyone.question: Does everyone have mood changes before a period?
everyone.answer: No. Premenstrual symptoms differ between people and may change over time.

diagnosis.question: Can mood logging diagnose PMS or PMDD?
diagnosis.answer: No. A log may help a healthcare professional understand timing and impact, but it is not a diagnostic test.

daily.question: Do I have to log my mood every day?
daily.answer: No. Choose a routine you find useful. Notes from different kinds of days can give you more to discuss, but you do not need a perfect record to ask for support.
